pages.text: $(flavor)From an ORSA orbital geology brief.$()$(br2)The ice sheet loads the crust. Along old seams it forces hot brine, steam and sulfur melt back up.

pages.title: Where
pages.text: Satellites saw new heat blooms most under snow belts, taiga and glacial basins.$(br2)They are natural ground features, not structures.

pages.title: Vent Classes
pages.text: $(bold)Dormant$(): mineral basin, faint bleed$(br)$(bold)Warm$(): brief warmth from Phase 6$(br)$(bold)Active$(): stable heat, geysers$(br)$(bold)Rupture$(): $(danger)growing cone, sulfur lava, ejecta, ashfall$()

pages.title: Field Guidance
pages.text: $(li)Warm: temporary refuge$(li)Active: risky shelter$(li)Rupture: survive around it, $(danger)not on it$()

pages.title: Spotting Vents
pages.text: A $(l:orsa_equipment/surveyor_lens)Surveyor Lens$(/l) sees only exposed heat, steam and hot crust.$(br2)Buried vents stay hidden until the ground opens.

Mature rupture mouths carry sulfur crust, friable tuff and heavy yellow deposits. The basin was too unstable to mine routinely.$(br2)$(danger)If the ground shakes in vacuum, the pressure column is about to move.$()
